newsitem.title: FRANCE: France hails Lebanese poll, Gemayel condemns it.
newsitem.headline: France hails Lebanese poll, Gemayel condemns it.

text.p: France on Monday hailed elections in Lebanon as a new step towards rebuilding the country, while former president Amin Gemayel called them a sham and took issue with Paris and Washington for endorsing them.

French Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said the polls were a positive step towards reconstructing Lebanon, and France hoped reconciliation would continue with respect for the country's unity, security and independence.

Gemayel, who now lives in France, said in a statement that there had been widespread fraud, and the results of the polls, whatever they were, could only be suspicious because of the overwhelming presence of Syrian troops.

Voters went to the polls in the eastern Bekaa valley on Sunday to elect the last 23 members in the 128-member parliament after voting in Mount Lebanon, the north, Beirut and the south on the past four Sundays.
"The turnout has been higher than in the previous election, which is in itself an encouraging factor," Rummelhardt told reporters.
Lebanese Interior Minister Michel al-Murr put turnout in the Bekaa at about 52 percent and said it was higher than in any other region.
Official results were expected later on Monday.

Gemayel said Syria, which has 35,000 troops in Lebanon, had not spared any pressure to achieve a high turnout. He said the aim of the election was to create a pro-Syrian parliament and crush Lebanese sovereignty.
"It is regrettable that some countries, including France and the United States, which champion democratic and liberal values...have endorsed this sham elections," he said.
